solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Possibly question our ersatz gemstone (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged another way

blocks.note: Q is a standard abbreviation for question
anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A jeweller casts doubt on a gem that looks like a fake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ersatz' looks like the anagram indicator, but its letters are needed; 'Possibly' does the stirring.
annotation.definitionFit: Rose quartz is a pink variety of quartz used as a gemstone.

entries.clue: Split first part of the tree up (4)

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of 'the'
in a down entry, going up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: the first letter of 'the'
a fir is a tree

annotation.surface: A tree splits from the base upward.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests splitting a trunk, but 'tree' is just FIR and 'up' turns T plus FIR round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a crack in rock or a breach between friends, both senses of the noun split.

entries.clue: Something fishy in second completed reshuffle (5-2)

indicators.note: puts the fish inside the other letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
'time's up' means time is completed
a hake is a fish

annotation.surface: A suspicious smell hangs over a finished cabinet reshuffle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' reads as a hint of scandal, but it is literally a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a reorganisation, such as a cabinet reshuffle.

entries.clue: A noble’s quite revolutionary? It’s doubtful (12)

indicators.note: the letters are turned over into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether an aristocrat could really be a revolutionary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to describe the noble, but it only tells you to rearrange the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Something questionable is open to doubt.

entries.clue: Delayed, putting off day to get joined in marriage (6)

indicators.note: putting something off can mean taking it off, like a coat, so the D for day is shed

blocks.note: to dally is to delay; the D for day is removed
D is the abbreviation for day; it is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A couple kept postponing the wedding day before finally marrying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting off' looks like part of the delaying story, but here it means taking the D off DALLIED.
annotation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned sense: two royal houses united through a wedding were said to be linked this way.

entries.clue: Final character of garment badly treated? (8)

definitions.text: Final character of garment badly treated?

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, in a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of 'garment'
anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A question about how the end of a piece of clothing got ruined.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a garment that has been badly treated ends up tattered.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue describes worn-out clothing in ragged shreds, which is exactly the answer's sense.

entries.clue: Box mostly surplus to requirements (4)

indicators.note: keeps most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: spare means surplus to requirements; its last letter E goes

annotation.surface: A carton that is largely unneeded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Box' reads as a container, but here it is the verb: to spar is to box.
annotation.definitionFit: A boxing term: boxers throw practice punches at a partner in the ring before a real bout.

entries.clue: Be in charge and live under pressure (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the second part sits beneath the first

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
to reside is to live somewhere

annotation.surface: Being the boss means living under constant pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint about leadership; in the grid, 'under' simply stacks RESIDE below P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the chair of a meeting or a judge in court runs the proceedings.

entries.clue: Contemplative Persian poet born here (10)

blocks.note: Rumi was a 13th-century Persian poet
a native is someone born here

annotation.surface: A thoughtful Persian poet was born in this very place.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a guidebook note about a poet's birthplace.
annotation.definitionFit: Ruminative means given to deep thought, contemplative.

entries.clue: Flog prisoner in cruel castle regularly (10)

indicators.note: puts the prisoner inside the word for cruel
something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at even steps: every second one

blocks.note: fell is an old word for cruel or fierce
an old lag is a long-serving prisoner
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of castle

annotation.surface: A prisoner is whipped in a brutal fortress.
annotation.walkthrough: Fell meaning cruel survives only in the phrase 'one fell swoop', so 'cruel' is easy to misread as an adjective for the castle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Latin for whip, used of penitents who whipped themselves.

entries.clue: Broadcast live in the morning (4)

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
a.m. marks times in the morning

annotation.surface: A breakfast show going out live.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live' and 'broadcast' look like one TV phrase, but 'live' is the verb BE.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: a signal is sent out on a beam, so to transmit a programme by radio or satellite is to send it that way.

entries.clue: Leading place to eat outside a home is sustainable (12)

indicators.note: the eating place goes around the other letters

blocks.note: main means leading or chief
you eat at a table
A as printed
in means at home

annotation.surface: A top restaurant around the corner is said to be eco-friendly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Home' means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'; 'Leading place to eat' looks like one phrase for a top restaurant but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: Something maintainable can be kept going, i.e. sustained.

entries.clue: Group of poets with half of Dante’s inspiration and creation (4,10)

indicators.note: keeps the first half of the name

blocks.note: Beatrice was Dante's muse; half of BEATRICE is BEAT
generation is the act of creating

annotation.surface: A literary circle claims to share Dante's muse and creativity.
annotation.walkthrough: Dante's inspiration is Beatrice, the woman he wrote about in the Divine Comedy.
annotation.definitionFit: The Beat Generation were the American poets and writers around Ginsberg and Kerouac.

entries.clue: Who’s got well within lock and key, right? (10)

definitions.text: Who’s got well within lock and key, right?

indicators.note: puts the well inside the lock

blocks.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a mineral spring, a well
E is a musical key
R is the abbreviation for right

annotation.surface: A question about someone who has got deep inside a locked property.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a trespasser: someone who got well inside despite the lock and key.
annotation.definitionFit: A trespasser is someone who has got onto property where they have no right to be.

entries.clue: Dinosaur ultimately with a power to run? (6)

definitions.text: Dinosaur ultimately with a power to run?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the end of Dinosaur is used

blocks.note: the last letter of Dinosaur
A as printed
P is the abbreviation for power
TO as printed
R is run in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A dinosaur finally given the power to run.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a fast, running predator dinosaur, while each word also supplies letters in order; 'to' is simply TO.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: raptors such as the velociraptor were agile two-legged dinosaurs built for running down prey.

entries.clue: What some do to the wheel? Check where the air goes (8)

definitions.text: What some do to the wheel?

blocks.note: to rein in is to check
air escapes through a vent

annotation.surface: Tips about a wheel: check where the air goes into the tyre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reinvent the wheel' is the idiom for wastefully redoing something already solved; the tyre picture hides it.
annotation.definitionFit: Some people reinvent the wheel, redoing what already works.

entries.clue: He tangled with the mob, a monstrous thing (8)

indicators.note: HE is mixed up together with THE MOB

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A man picked a fight with the gangsters and met a monster.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a gangster story; HE and THE MOB are simply rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A behemoth is something enormous and monstrous, after the biblical beast.

entries.clue: Traveller a long way away in south at all times (8)

indicators.note: something a long way away is in another place, so this phrase sits inside the word for always

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
e'er is the poetic short form of ever
afar means a long way off

annotation.surface: A traveller who is always far away down south.
annotation.walkthrough: The poetic contraction e'er for ever is a crossword regular; 'in south' tempts you to put something inside S, but S simply leads.
annotation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a sailor, one who travels by sea.

entries.clue: After a fake, news chief is red-faced (7)

indicators.note: the editor comes after A SHAM

blocks.note: A as printed
a sham is a fake
ED is short for editor, head of a newspaper

annotation.surface: An editor is embarrassed after running a fake story.
annotation.walkthrough: ED for editor is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: shame makes you blush, so red-faced stands for the feeling itself.

entries.clue: Sweet, tailless dogs were trained by this man (6)

definitions.text: dogs were trained by this man

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, so a tailless sweet has lost its final A

blocks.note: pavlova is a meringue dessert; its last A goes

annotation.surface: Dogs without tails were trained with sweets by this man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' seems to describe the dogs, but it docks the dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov conditioned dogs to salivate at a signal.

entries.clue: Concern when oaf takes in nothing very well (7)

indicators.note: the oaf holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: a lout is an oaf
O looks like zero, nothing
OK means very well, as in agreement

annotation.surface: A worry arises when a clumsy man understands nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concern' is the sense in 'that's your lookout', meaning your own business.
annotation.definitionFit: 'That's your lookout' means that's your concern.

entries.clue: Way mastic perhaps is worked into stone (6)

indicators.note: mastic is only one example of a tree
the tree is fitted inside the stone

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
the mastic is a Mediterranean tree

annotation.surface: A mason works mastic resin into a stone.
annotation.walkthrough: Mastic sounds like a putty, but it is also the tree that yields the resin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym seen in road names: Way, like Street, is a common suffix for a thoroughfare.

entries.clue: Area coldest, close against part of leg (8,6)

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
chillest means coldest
the close is the end
leaning on means against

annotation.surface: The coldest area is right up against the leg.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like the adjective near, but it is the noun meaning end.
annotation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscle to the heel.

entries.clue: Image of no king one put up (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: NO as printed
K is king in chess
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A portrait of a man who is no king, hung on the wall.
annotation.walkthrough: IKON is a variant spelling of icon.
annotation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of icon, the painted religious image of Orthodox churches.

entries.clue: What comes before the final house? (4)

blocks.note: in a knockout contest, the round just before the final
British slang for a house joined to its neighbour by one shared wall

annotation.surface: A riddle about which house comes just before the last one on the street.
annotation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall.
annotation.definitionFit: Semi is short for both semi-final and semi-detached house.

entries.clue: Building in city to secure housing plan that’s had backing (5,5)

indicators.note: TO and LOCK hold the plan between them
the plan is written backwards

blocks.note: TO as printed
to brew is to plan or plot; reversed it is WERB
to lock is to secure

annotation.surface: A city building project that has secured financial backing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like funding for the housing plan, but it reverses BREW.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the tall block of flats is a typical urban building, hence 'in city'.

entries.clue: Disrespectful rough dismissing Conservative (4)

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the Conservative is sacked from the word for rough

blocks.note: crude means rough; its C goes
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party

annotation.surface: A rough type rudely dismisses a Tory.
annotation.walkthrough: C for Conservative is a standard abbreviation for the British party.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: impolite behaviour shows a lack of respect.

entries.clue: Keep talking about poet’s end? This one’s was tragic (10)

indicators.note: about can mean around, so the phrase for keep talking wraps around the poet's last letter

blocks.note: to chatter on is to keep talking
the last letter of poet

annotation.surface: Rambling on about a poet's death, which was a tragedy.
annotation.walkthrough: Thomas Chatterton was an 18th-century English poet who poisoned himself at 17; 'this one' is the poet just mentioned.
annotation.definitionFit: Chatterton's end was famously tragic: he died by suicide at seventeen.
